units.translation: To pour wine as a libation. And perhaps this is natural. For since Hermes is traditionally said to be reason, and his instrument is the tongue, which rests when sleep falls, they fittingly sacrifice it to Hermes. And Homer (Od. 3.332): 'But come, cut out the tongues' instead of 'stop your speeches.'

c. Themis is: Dieuchidas in his Megarian History (FGrH 8 M. IV 390) relates that Alcathous, son of Pelops, exiled from Mycenae because of the murder of Chrysippus, was on his way to settle in another city. When he encountered a lion ravaging Megara, against which others had also been sent by the king of Megara, he overcame it and, placing its tongue in a pouch, went back to Megara. And when those sent on the hunt reported that they were the ones who had overcome it, he brought forward the pouch and exposed them. Therefore the king, after sacrificing to the gods, finally placed the tongue on the altars, and from then on this custom remained among the Megarians. Philochorus in his On Sacrifices (FGrH 173 M. I 413) says that it is the finest and foremost part of the body. And Homer (Od. 3.341): 'they cast the tongues into the fire.'

d. [With enchantment:] In the preliminary edition after this is written: 'But when the third dawn appeared on that night, while they were feasting there on a sacrifice of oxen to the Far-shooter, then from Zeus a breeze fell, and Tiphys arose, bidding them to go aboard the benches. And they, hearing <...>.' Then after the quoted lines: 'and dreadfully the harbor' (v. 524).

526-27. For in it a spear: plausibly he says that the speaking timber in the Argo is from the Dodonian oak, since that too spoke, as Homer says (Il. 14.327-8): 'so that he might hear the counsel of the god from the high-leafed oak.'

528. They upon the benches: the seats of the rowers, the rowing-benches. In general the broad plank is called a bench and a rowing-bench, whence we also call the columns of rhapsodies 'pages' because of their breadth.
532-33. With his feet he was washed under: and as he sat upon it, the keel of the ship was washed from below rather at his feet and went into the depth of the sea by the weight of the hero.
